ETHICS ADVISORY OPINION NO. 26-004-E
March 6, 2026
Question Presented: May a former city council member serve without compensation on
the city planning commission within one year of leaving office on
the city council?
Brief Answer: Yes. Because the former city council member will receive no
compensation for serving on the city planning commission, no
contract will exist, and no violation of Section 109, Miss. Const. of
1890, or Section 25-4-105(2), Miss. Code of 1972, will result, even
within one year of leaving office on the city council.
The Mississippi Ethics Commission issued this opinion on the date shown above in
accordance with Section 25-4-17(i), Mississippi Code of 1972, as reflected upon its minutes of
even date. The Commission is empowered to interpret and opine only upon Article IV, Section
109, Mississippi Constitution of 1890, and Article 3, Chapter 4, Title 25, Mississippi Code of 1972.
This opinion does not interpret or offer protection from liability for any other laws, rules or
regulations. The Commission based this opinion solely on the facts and circumstances provided
by the requestor as restated herein. The protection from liability provided under Section 25-4-17(i)
is limited to the individual who requested this opinion and to the accuracy and completeness of
these facts.
I. LAW
The pertinent Ethics in Government Laws to be considered here are as follows:
Section 109, Miss. Const. of 1890.
No public officer or member of the legislature shall be interested, directly or
indirectly, in any contract with the state, or any district, county, city, or town
thereof, authorized by any law passed or order made by any board of which he may
be or may have been a member, during the term for which he shall have been
chosen, or within one year after the expiration of such term.

Section 25-4-103, Miss. Code of 1972.
(e) “Compensation” means money or thing of value received, or to be received,
from any person for services rendered.
(f) “Contract” means:
(i) Any agreement to which the government is a party; or
(ii) Any agreement on behalf of the government which involves the payment
of public funds.
(g) “Government” means the state and all political entities thereof, both collectively
and separately, including but not limited to:
(i) Counties;
(ii) Municipalities;
(iii) All school districts;
(iv) All courts; and
(v) Any department, agency, board, commission, institution,
instrumentality, or legislative or administrative body of the state, counties
or municipalities created by statute, ordinance or executive order including
all units that expend public funds.
(o) “Public funds” means money belonging to the government.
(p) “Public servant” means:
(i) Any elected or appointed official of the government;
(ii) Any officer, director, commissioner, supervisor, chief, head, agent or
employee of the government or any agency thereof, or of any public entity
created by or under the laws of the state of Mississippi or created by an
agency or governmental entity thereof, any of which is funded by public
funds or which expends, authorizes or recommends the use of public funds;
or
(iii) Any individual who receives a salary, per diem or expenses paid in
whole or in part out of funds authorized to be expended by the government.
Section 25-4-105, Miss. Code of 1972.
(2) No public servant shall be interested, directly or indirectly, during the term for
which he shall have been chosen, or within one (1) year after the expiration of such
term, in any contract with the state, or any district, county, city or town thereof,

II. FACTS
Facts provided by the requestor are set forth below, with identifying information redacted, and
are considered a part of this opinion.
Introduction and Summary Question:
As you know, I am general counsel to the City […]. In that capacity I have been
requested by [a] Council Member … to write for an official opinion from the Ethics
Commission. The question is whether a former City Council member may, within
one year after completing his term of office, be appointed to serve on a Board or
Commission of the City that is required by statute to be uncompensated for that
service. We ask this question to ensure that neither the Mayor and City Council nor
the former council member violates either Section 109 of the Mississippi
Constitution or Section 25-4-105(2) of the Mississippi Code both of which prohibit
public servants from being interested, directly or indirectly, during his or her term
of office, or within one year thereafter, in any contract with the city, authorized by
any order made by the board of which he was a member.
Factual Background:
Planning Commission: The City has an opening on its Planning Commission (" the
Commission"). The Commission recommends adoption of a comprehensive plan
of the City, has the power to commission studies and to recommend zoning plans
and changes to zoning as well as to recommend regulations related to development
of subdivisions and the cohesive development of the City. According to the City's
Ordinances establishing the Commission, its members, including any ex officio
members, may not receive compensation for their services on the Commission. See
§23-23 of the Code of Ordinances of the City….
Term of Office of Former Council Member: As you are probably aware, the City's
last general election was in 2025. The presently serving Mayor and City Council
were sworn in on July l, 2025 at 12:01 AM and the term of office of the outgoing
Council was June 30, 2025 at midnight. Thus, it has not yet been one year since the
prior City Council's administration ended. [A certain individual] was the Council
Member for Ward … of the City Council but was defeated in the general election,
and his term ended on June 30, 2025.
Applicant for Commission: [That former city council member] has applied to serve
on the Commission. As stated, [the former city council member] left office at
midnight on June 30, 2025. The appointment is up for consideration [very soon].
Obviously, if the Council were favorably inclined toward appointing [the former
city council member], they would like to have a prompt answer. My advice if the

majority of the Council is inclined toward appointing him would be to condition
his appointment upon an advance favorable Commission Opinion and that he wait
for same before taking his oath of office and serving.
Question Presented: The question therefore concisely stated is as follows: Does
either Section 109 or Section 25-4-105 prohibit [the former city council member]
from service on the Planning Commission during the 12 months that follow his exit
from office at midnight on June 30, 2025? Of course, we ask for an Official
Commission Opinion pursuant to Section 25-4-17. Please feel free to contact me
should you require additional information.
III. ANALYSIS
Section 109, Miss. Const. of 1890, and its statutory parallel, Section 25-4-105(2), Miss.
Code of 1972, prohibit a member of a public board from having any direct or indirect interest in a
contract funded or otherwise authorized by that board during his or her term or for one year
thereafter. Frazier v. State, ex rel. Pittman, 504 So.2d 675, 693 (Miss. 1987). Every public
employee has a contract of employment, many of which are oral, at-will contracts rather than
written contracts. Any employment contract which violates Section 109 or Section 25-4-105(2) is
null and void, and the employee can be liable to repay all money he receives. Towner v. Moore,
ex rel. Quitman County School District, 604 So.2d 1093, 1096 (Miss. 1992), quoting Smith v.
Dorsey, 530 So.2d 5, 9 (Miss. 1988). Consequently, a former city council member cannot be an
employee or contractor of the city within one year of leaving office.
With regard to a “public office,” there is no contract. Johnston v. Reeves & Co., 72 So.
925, 927 (Miss. 1916). Yet the Ethics Commission has previously found that members of
municipal planning commissions “do not exercise any sovereign power of the state and do not hold
a public office.” See Advisory Opinion No. 09-073-E. Moreover, if the former alderman were to
serve without compensation for one year after leaving office with the understanding or expectation
that such employment would thereafter continue with compensation, then the board would still be
authorizing a future contract with a former member in violation of Section 109 and Section 25-4-
105(2). See Advisory Opinions No. 25-035-E, 16-044-E and 09-059-E.
Municipalities are authorized by statute to compensate their planning commission
members with a per diem not to exceed “$120.00 in the aggregate per month.” Section 17-1-11.
Compensation could entail a contract between the municipality and the planning commission
member, which would violate Section 109 and Section 25-4-105(2) where the commission member
was on the city council less than one year prior. However, this city’s ordinance prohibits members
of the city planning commission from receiving any compensation. Because the former city council
member will receive no compensation for serving on the city planning commission, no contract
will exist, and no violation of Section 109 or Section 25-4-105(2) will result, even within one year
of leaving office on the city council.
